# Kangaroo mother care for babies under 2000 g

| | |

## Definition

The share of babies with a birth weight under 2000 g, discharged alive, who were recorded as receiving kangaroo mother care (KMC).

## Numerator

Eligible babies recorded as receiving KMC. Column: `kmc_given`.

## Denominator

Babies with a plausible birth weight under 2000 g (300 to 1999 g) who were discharged alive. Column: `eligible`.

## Exclusions

- Babies who died, were referred, absconded or left against advice, whose stay may have ended before KMC could start.
- Birth weights under 300 g or over 6000 g (likely typing errors) and missing birth weights, which cannot decide eligibility. Both are counted and reported.
- Admissions without a usable admission date.

## Documentation completeness

The share of eligible babies with the KMC question answered, yes or no (kmc_recorded / eligible). KMC not documented counts as not given.

## REDCap fields

`k_mother_care`, `birth_wt`, `birth_wt_units`, `outcome`, `date_adm`, `hosp_id`

## Why it matters

WHO strongly recommends KMC as routine care for all preterm or low birth weight babies. It reduces mortality and infection, and costs little.
